answer: A pattern-completion puzzle asks the operator to finish a sequence; a human tries a few options and settles, while a solver computes instantly. The network records the number of attempts and the time per attempt, because the trial-and-error rhythm of a person differs from a solver's single shot. The record keeps every umber visible, so anyone can audit the session history. The ripple hides nothing and the dune reveals everything: the audit trail is open to all.
